units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
Why have you never spoken of this in writing to me?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: I have never before seen it in such a light that I could speak of it to you, his son.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: In what light did you see it, then?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Slowly.
I saw only this one thing: that your father was a broken-down man before you were born.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Softly.
Ah--!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: He rises and walks away to the window.
And then; day after day, I dwelt on the one thought that by rights Regina should be at home in this house--just like my own boy.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Turning round quickly.
Regina--!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Springs up and asks, with bated breath.
Yes, now you know it, both of you.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Regina!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: To herself.
So mother was that kind of woman.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Your mother had many good qualities, Regina.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, but she was one of that sort, all the same. Oh, I've often suspected it; but--And now, if you please, ma'am, may I be allowed to go away at once?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Do you really wish it, Regina?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, indeed I do.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Of course you can do as you like; but--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Goes towards REGINA.
Go away now? Your place is here.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Merci , Mr. Alving!--or now, I suppose, I may say Oswald. But I can tell you this wasn't at all what I expected.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Regina, I have not been frank with you--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: No, that you haven't indeed. If I'd known that Oswald was an invalid, why--And now, too, that it can never come to anything serious between us--I really can't stop out here in the country and wear myself out nursing sick people.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Not even one who is so near to you?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: No, that I can't. A poor girl must make the best of her young days, or she'll be left out in the cold before she knows where she is. And I, too, have the joy of life in me, Mrs. Alving!
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Unfortunately, you leave. But don't throw yourself away, Regina.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Oh, what must be, must be. If Oswald takes after his father, I take after my mother, I daresay.--May I ask, ma'am, if Pastor Manders knows all this about me?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Pastor Manders knows all about it.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Busied in putting on her shawl.

Well then, I'd better make haste and get away by this steamer. The Pastor is such a nice man to deal with; and I certainly think I've as much right to a little of that money as he has--that brute of a carpenter.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: You are heartily welcome to it, Regina.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Looks hard at her.
I think you might have brought me up as a gentleman's daughter, ma'am; it would have suited me better.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Tosses her head.
But pooh--what does it matter!
units.name: REGINA

units.text: With a bitter side glance at the corked bottle.
I may come to drink champagne with gentlefolks yet.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: And if you ever need a home, Regina, come to me.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: No, thank you, ma'am. Pastor Manders will look after me, I know. And if the worst comes to the worst, I know of one house where I've every right to a place.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Where is that?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: "Chamberlain Alving's Home."
units.name: REGINA
